'''Lan-Hsuan Huang''' ({{lang-zh|黃籃萱}}) is a Taiwanese-American mathematician and [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] specializing in [[differential geometry]], [[geometric analysis]], and their applications in the [[theory of relativity]].{{r|shape}} She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Connecticut]]. Huang serves on the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]]''.

==Education and career==
Huang majored in mathematics at [[National Taiwan University]], graduating in 2004.{{r|cv}} She went to [[Stanford University]] for graduate study in mathematics, and completed her Ph.D. there in 2009. Her doctoral dissertation, ''Center of Mass and Constant Mean Curvature Foliations for Isolated Systems'', was supervised by [[Richard Schoen]].{{r|cv|mg}}

After three years at [[Columbia University]] as Joseph F. Ritt Assistant Professor of Mathematics, she joined the Department of Mathematics <ref>[https://math.uconn.edu/  UConn Mathematics Department]</ref> at the [[University of Connecticut]] in 2012 as a tenure-track  assistant professor. She was promoted to associate professor in 2016, and to full professor in 2020.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
In 2018, Huang was named a Simons Fellow<ref name=SimonsF>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees Simons Fellows]</ref>  in mathematics and  a von Neumann Fellow<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/lan-hsuan-huang von Neumann Fellows]</ref> at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].{{r|cv}} She was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2024 class of fellows.{{r|fams}} She was awarded a Simons Fellowship again in 2025.<ref name=SimonsF/>
